explicit_validation.explanation: Both LLM-as-a-judge and human evaluation are conducted but they are used for different purposes (LLM for filtering commonsense relevance, human for response/dialogue quality) and no quantitative comparison or validation between LLM and human judgments is reported.

prompts.notes: LLM was used as a zero-shot classifier via three-way multiple choice questions (yes/no/unknown) to validate whether commonsense triples were meaningfully instantiated, but exact prompt templates are not explicitly shown in the provided text.

guidelines.notes: Human judges compare dialogues/responses in head-to-head comparisons based on specific criteria; guidelines include examples (e.g., annotation page shown in Figure) but detailed scoring rubrics are not fully described in the main text.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM evaluations focus on validating commonsense triple instantiation in narratives/conversations, while human evaluations assess dialogue and response quality along multiple conversational dimensions. There is no overlap in criteria between the two evaluation methods.
